title: Digital Edition Introductions, Editorial Principles & Multi-Modal Publication
query: What scholarly conventions govern the introduction, stemma codicum, and editorial rationale of a digital critical edition, and what technical standards enable dual web and print publication from TEI XML sources?

results.title: 5.5 Criticisms of digital methods
results.authors_venue_year: [PDF][PDF] 5.5 Criticisms of digital methodsJB Guillaumin - Handbook of Stemmatology, 2020 - library.oapen.orgDiscusses scholarly conventions and standards developed for print editions over two centuries and examines how the digital paradigm challenges and suggests changes to these conventions.Forms of Digital Publication: Explores different forms of digital publication, including digital editions that must also be published in print, and those designed for online use, which implies discussion of technical standards for dual publication.Stemma Production and Display: Mentions that phylogenetic methods often produce a bifurcating tree for the stemma, sometimes intentionally simplifying the model, and notes that the stemma must depict cases fundamental for the *eliminatio codicum descriptorum*.Save Cite Cited by 8 Related articles All 8 versions  No full text available View as HTML [PDF] oapen.org

results.title: 6.3 Representing the critical text
results.authors_venue_year: [PDF][PDF] 6.3 Representing the critical textF Fischer - Handbook of Stemmatology, 2020 - library.oapen.orgDetails the traditional components of a philological introduction for a critical edition, including descriptions of textual witnesses, genealogical analysis, and a declaration of editorial principles, which are extended in a digital setting to include facsimiles, transcriptions, source code, and raw data.Stemma Codicum Conventions: Notes that digital critical editions, unlike traditional print editions, challenge established conventions regarding the stemma codicum, with some editors refraining from creating one or even publishing a progressive edition before establishing one.Print Publication from Digital Sources: Mentions the use of LaTeX, specifically the reledmac package, for typesetting scholarly critical editions that adhere to print presentation standards, suggesting a technical solution for dual print publication from digital sources, though the snippet does not explicitly mention TEI XML.Save Cite Cited by 10 Related articles All 8 versions  No full text available View as HTML

results.title: Digital Scholarly Editing in Practice: Making Oxford University Voltaire
results.authors_venue_year: [BOOK][B] Digital Scholarly Editing in Practice: Making Oxford University VoltaireD Barker, N Cronk, G Roe - 2026 - cambridge.orgExplains that digital scholarly editions (DSEs) utilize traditional critical editing methodologies alongside contemporary technological innovation to represent texts in new ways.Stemma and Editorial Rationale: Notes that constructing a stemma codicum traces the relationships between different manuscript witnesses, while eclectic editing involves selecting the 'best' readings to build an ideal text.TEI-XML Standards: Establishes that the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI) has become the standard for encoding texts in a structured, machine-readable format, enabling interoperability and preservation through open standards like TEI-XML.Save Cite Cited by 1 Related articles All 2 versions  [PDF] uinsyahada.ac.id

results.title: Digital Scholarly Editing
results.authors_venue_year: [PDF][PDF] Digital Scholarly EditingMJ Driscoll, E Pierazzo - Theories and Practices, 2016 - oer.uinsyahada.ac.idDiscusses the need to reconceive the systemic triplet of textual criticism, editing, and edition in important respects in terms of the digital medium, as the scholarly edition will increasingly live in the digital medium.Editorial Rationale and Introduction: Explains that the argument, or rationale, for the edition is given in the Editorial Introduction, which is part of an aggregate of discourses held together by a common reference grid.TEI XML and Visualization: Mentions that Edition Visualization Technology (EVT) is a software tool created to navigate and visualize digital editions based on the TEI XML encoding standard, which is relevant to the dual web and print publication of TEI XML sources.Save Cite Cited by 143 Related articles All 17 versions  View as HTML [PDF] hal.science

results.title: Digital scholarly editing: Theories, models and methods

results.title: Creating a digital critical edition of a classical text with XML/TEI
results.authors_venue_year: Creating a digital critical edition of a classical text with XML/TEIF Lazzerini, M Di Franco - Umanistica Digitale, 2026 - iris.unito.itDiscusses scholarly conventions used in traditional critical editions, such as the editor’s task to reconstruct the most likely version of the text (constitutio textus) and the Lachmannian principle of eliminatio codicum descriptorum for selecting variants.Editorial Rationale Visibility: Explains that a digital critical edition encoded with XML/TEI can embed a deep semantic layer to realize the advantage of representing the editorial reasoning in a dynamic, customizable way.Technical Standards: Identifies TEI XML as the de facto standard markup language for digital editions in the humanities, noting that a digital edition cannot be given in print without significant loss of content and functionality, which suggests limitations for dual publication.Save Cite Related articles All 3 versions  No full text available View as HTML [HTML] acm.org
